summary: Stevens County, WA lookout on First Thought Mountain near Orient: steel tower with L-4 cab 1947; cab moved to Orient Community Park in 1986; site today not described.

facts.design: 40-foot steel Aermotor tower with L-4 cab (1947)
facts.status_note: Cab moved to Orient Community Park in 1986 (register text and Weebly). No source describes the mountain site today.

events.note: Newspaper report of a station recently constructed on First Thought Hill near Orient (quoted on Weebly). Register dates the first lookout to 1916.
Register: 35-foot pole platform with a log shelter at the base
Stanley Pierce has the lookout station (Weebly, Republic News-Miner)
Register: 60-foot pole tower with 6x6 cab. Weebly: 70-foot wooden tower built that April, 76 feet to the roof. The sources disagree on height.
Walter Spaid named as the man chosen to serve as lookout (Weebly)
Keith Miller took charge of the lookout station (Weebly)
Concrete poured for the footings of a steel tower with an L-4 cab
40-foot steel tower with L-4 cab completed. Weebly says it was recycled from a parachute training tower in Idaho; no second source found.
Marilyn Buck on First Thought lookout tower (Weebly)
Ernie Keyes listed for 1958 and 1959 (Firelookout list of known personnel)
Orient Improvement Clubs purchased the lookout, planning to move it to Orient Community Park
Cab set onto a trailer by crane and moved to Orient Community Park. Register photo caption says 2001.

corrections.why: The 70-foot figure belongs to the 1925 wooden tower. The steel tower the cab sat on from 1947 was 40 feet (register and Weebly).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the first lookout to 1916 (35-foot pole platform). Weebly quotes an August 1914 newspaper item about a station recently built. Both are reported; the story says the 1914 item is a newspaper report.
The register gives a 60-foot pole tower with a 6x6 cab. Weebly quotes a 70-foot wooden tower, 76 feet to the roof after enclosure. Not reconciled; both are reported.
The register text and Weebly both give 1986. The register photo caption gives 2001 without explanation. The story follows the 1986 text.
Weebly quotes Stanley Pierce for 1920 and Stanley Pearce for 1921. Which spelling is correct is not confirmed.

notes_for_editor: Today's status is not verified. The Waymarking listing for the cab (wm14EZ5) returned only its title through fetch_text, so it is not cited. A search snippet for that listing and an Orient park listing suggest the cab is still in the park, but I could not read either page in full. Reading one of them would settle the present condition. The height correction is proposed because the brief's 21.3 m matches the 1925 70-foot tower, not the 1947 40-foot steel tower. The steel tower's Idaho origin rests on Weebly alone. Staffing names come from the Weebly page and the Firelookout list of known personnel, which is not complete, so no facts.staffing is recorded. Reads: 2 websearch.py queries and 6 page reads, including one guessed Orient URL that returned 404 and one Waymarking page that returned only its title.
